test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 7800 litres in 12 hours and 10 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 8800 litres?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate of **Pipe A** = 7800 ÷ 12 = 650 litres/hr

Rate of **Pipe B** = 7800 ÷ 12 = 780 litres/hr

Combined Rate = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hr

Time to fill 8800 litres = 8800 ÷ 1430 = 880 ÷ 143 = 80/13 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 80/13 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Capacity 1 = 7800 litres, Time A = 12 hrs, Time B = 10 hrs, Target Capacity = 8800 litres.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Work ÷ Time; Time = Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hrs)**
 **Base Work (litres)**
 **Efficiency (litres/hr)**

 **A**
 12

 **B**
 10

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B) = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hr

⇒ Target Work = 8800 litres

⇒ Required Time = 8800 ÷ 1430

⇒ Required Time = 880/143

⇒ Required Time = (80 × 11) ÷ (13 × 11) = 80/13 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 80/13 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time when work is constant. If an **inlet pipe** fills a tank in 'x' hours, its work done in 1 hour is 1/x.

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

**Inlet pipes** perform positive work while **outlet pipes** (leakage) perform negative work. Net efficiency = Σ(Inlet Efficiency) − Σ(Outlet Efficiency).

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B in y hours, they together fill in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours for the **same total work**.</p
